Subject: Cost & model-mix validation: PriCorp POC — next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clarity on the PriCorp use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock pricing and the model routing for the POC.

Call highlights (very short):
- Primary feature: document ingestion -> retrieval + chat assistant + rerank for automated triage.
- Expected steady-state: ~45M LLM tokens / month (inference tokens), +/- 20%.
- Embedding traffic: ~150k vector queries/day concentrated during business hours.
- Latency target: 300–500ms for chat-first-turn, 100–200ms for embed lookups (not a hard SLO today, just a target).

Initial cost & model-mix proposal (for validation):
- Target unit economics we're shooting for: $7k / 1M tokens (ballpark for blended traffic).
- Suggested model split (inference volume): Chat responses 70% (most calls -> MPT-chat-variant or small LLM), Embedding generation 25% (sparse batchable), Rerank 5% (low-volume, high-accuracy).
- Operational levers: batching for embeddings (daytime bursts), prefix caching for common prompts, and quantized rerank models to control GPU cost.

Attachments: pricing-estimate.xlsx (high-level monthly cost scenarios for 3 model mixes).

Asks: can you confirm:
1) the ~45M tokens/month and 150k embed queries/day are in the right neighborhood?
2) an initial budget range you feel comfortable committing to for the POC (monthly committed spend helps us reserve Dedicated capacity).

If those numbers hold, Rishi will draft a tight unit-econ sketch and a two-option model routing plan (conservative vs aggressive) tomorrow. Recommend a 30-minute follow-up on Wed to finalize procurement path.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cost & model-mix validation: PriCorp POC — next steps

Thanks, Jasmine — good summary. Quick clarifications from our side:
- The 45M tokens/month is our current best estimate based on October–December traffic, could swing down to ~36M or up to ~55M depending on retention.
- Embeddings: 150k/day is correct; these are mostly search-fresh queries (we may add caching later).
- Budget: priors from procurement suggest a comfortable POC monthly band of $6k–$9k to start; if economics are demonstrably better we can expand.
- Latency: 300–500ms for initial reply is acceptable, anything over 800ms may degrade user satisfaction.

Question for pricing: how do you calculate the $/1M token blended figure when embedding queries are priced differently (per-embed) and rerank is per-call? Can you send a worked example mapping our volumes to an expected monthly invoice?

Also, who on Redwood will be our procurement contact for the MSA and billing questions? Sarah in procurement will want a point of contact.

Best,
Amit
Head of Data Platform, FinServ.ai
amit@finserv.ai

Subject: Re: Cost & model-mix validation: PriCorp POC — next steps

Amit — thanks for the questions. Attaching a quick unit-econ sketch (unit-econ-breakdown.pdf) and two sample invoice scenarios matching the traffic buckets Jasmine called out. High level notes:

- Blended $/1M tokens: we compute this as (sum of model-specific token cost * tokens per model + embedding cost + rerank calls cost) / total tokens, normalized to 1M. For transparency we show per-model TP token price and per-embed price in the attachment.

- With the sample mix (Chat 70 / Embed 25 / Rerank 5), and using our hosted catalog midrange instances, a plausible monthly invoice for 45M tokens + 150k embeds/day falls into the $6.5k–$8k band depending on cache hit rates and batching. That maps to the $7k / 1M tokens blended number Jasmine used.

- If you want to push costs further down we can:
  * route low-latency small prompts to cheaper quantized chat variants,
  * aggressively batch embeddings in 1-minute windows to reduce I/O overhead,
  * convert rerank to a smaller distill model for the initial POC.

- Operational ask: if procurement wants committed spend, recommend a 3-month reserved capacity agreement for a modest discount and guaranteed throughput. We can draft two commitment tiers for Sarah to review.

Procurement contact: Monica will own the MSA/billing thread and coordinate with your team; Monica — can you pick this up with Sarah?

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
